why: The four Python hooks are not one component, and honest answers differ per file. The property no alternative provides is EVIDENCE BOUND TO A CONTENT HASH OF THE WORKING TREE: ship_gate_stop.py:154-186 accepts a done-claim only when state/gate-runs.jsonl holds a non-partial PASS whose fingerprint equals gate.tree_fingerprint(project) right now, and pre_push_gate.py:167-209 accepts a push only when every passing check inside .claude/proofs/current.json carries the same git_commit AND diff_sha256 the tree has this instant. The closest thing found in the wild, MPIsaac-Per/claude-code-loop-patterns 04-stop-hook, does exactly this job with a RECENCY window (MAX_AGE_MINUTES, default 30) instead of a hash, confirmed by fetching its README -- which means under it a proof earned at minute 0 still authorises a claim about code edited at minute 29, the precise failure both of these hooks exist to prevent. TDD Guard/Probity, Invariant Guardrails, NeMo Guardrails and AgentSpec all enforce at the action boundary and none of them models 'this evidence was earned against a different tree'. So keep those two files (543 of the 791 lines). But the other two do not survive the same scrutiny. safety_gate.py is 17 regexes over a raw command string and I measured its gap rather than asserting it: feeding it `T=/ ; rm -rf $T` and `eval $(echo payload | base64 -d)` returns an allow, while the literal forms are denied -- and claude-code-bash-guardian (MIT) already parses commands to a bashlex AST specifically to close variable-indirection and wrapper cases. Its POSIX branch should be backed by an AST parse; only the PowerShell/cmd branch (Remove-Item -Recurse, rd /s, %USERPROFILE%, drive-letter paths) has no off-the-shelf equivalent, because every OSS guard found is Unix-only. And completion_gate.py's 74 lines are already convicted by their own sibling: ship_gate_stop.py:4-11 says in writing that searching the assistant's sentence for the word 'tested' passes an agent that writes 'implemented and tested' whether or not anything ran. That file is a nudge, not a gate, and the audit should say so rather than shelter it under the two files that do real work.

alternatives.name: MPIsaac-Per/claude-code-loop-patterns, pattern 04-stop-hook (no_completion_without_evidence.py, GitHub)
alternatives.covers: the exact job of ship_gate_stop.py: a Stop hook that reads the event JSON from stdin, resolves the project via event['cwd'], looks for verification evidence, emits {"decision":"block","reason":...} when it is absent, and carries the same stop_hook_active reentrancy guard (ship_gate_stop.py:201-202). Pure stdlib Python, no dependencies -- a drop-in shape match.
alternatives.gap: it validates evidence by RECENCY ONLY. Confirmed by fetching the pattern's README: evidence under .evidence/ counts if it is newer than MAX_AGE_MINUTES (default 30), and 'a newer failed or malformed record invalidates an older successful record'. There is no git commit, no diff hash, no working-tree fingerprint anywhere in its model, so it cannot distinguish 'proof for this tree' from 'proof for the tree as it was before the last four edits' -- which is the single property ship_gate_stop.py:172-186 exists to enforce. It also has no equivalent of the fail-loud branch at ship_gate_stop.py:210-214 (announce that enforcement is OFF when the runner is unreachable), the deliberate answer to the twelve one-line dead hooks sitting in this same directory that point at /home/shovalbe/.codex/hooks/ and fail open silently on a Windows machine.
alternatives.cost: free, stdlib Python, no install; would REMOVE a dependency on tools/gate/gate.py
alternatives.maturity: not verified. I fetched the pattern directory and read its README; no licence, no last-commit date and no star count were visible in what I fetched. I did not read its source, and I did not check whether the repo is maintained.

alternatives.name: claude-code-bash-guardian (RoaringFerrum, GitHub, MIT)
alternatives.covers: the job of safety_gate.py, and covers it with a better mechanism: it parses each Bash command into an AST with bashlex instead of regex-matching the string, and advertises heredoc preprocessing, wrapper-command detection (sudo, xargs, timeout), variable-command prevention, path-traversal blocking and a configurable blacklist. This directly addresses the completeness gap safety_gate.py:6-8 admits about itself in its own docstring.
alternatives.gap: Unix only -- its docs mention no Windows, PowerShell or cmd support, and bashlex parses POSIX shell, so it cannot see `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force C:\Users\shova` or `rd /s %USERPROFILE%` at all. Those are three of safety_gate.py's seventeen rules (safety_gate.py:29-47) and this is a Windows-primary machine whose default shell is PowerShell. It also carries none of the credential-exfiltration rules (safety_gate.py:105-138, three patterns that stop `cat .env`, `rg .ssh/id_ed25519`, and an interpreter one-liner reading a .pem into model-visible output) and no git-history-destruction rules (safety_gate.py:48-100, ten patterns covering reset --hard, clean -f, checkout --, restore, switch --discard-changes, forced/mirror/refspec push).
alternatives.cost: MIT, pip/conda/poetry installable, but adds PyYAML + bashlex to a currently zero-dependency stdlib hook that must start in under a 5s timeout (dot-claude/settings.json PreToolUse timeout: 5) on every single Bash call
alternatives.maturity: weak, and this is the reason not to adopt it wholesale: I fetched the repo page and it shows 7 stars and 3 total commits. I did not verify its last commit date, did not install it, and did not run it against the two commands my own probe showed safety_gate.py allowing, so its claimed variable-command prevention is unverified by me.

alternatives.name: Probity (nizos/probity, npm @nizos/probity, MIT) -- successor to nizos/tdd-guard
alternatives.covers: the enforcement job of completion_gate.py and part of pre_push_gate.py, properly: it intercepts file writes and shell commands before execution across Claude Code, Codex and Copilot CLI, blocks rule violations, and explains the violation to the agent. Rules can be deterministic (string/regex on command or file content) OR AI-validated through the vendor SDK the agent is already authenticated with -- which is a strictly better version of completion_gate.py's regex-vs-regex wording check, since a model can judge whether a claim is actually backed rather than whether the token 'tested' appears.
alternatives.gap: no git working-tree hash and no evidence ledger -- I asked the fetch specifically about this and the repo content surfaced neither, so it cannot express 'this proof was earned against a different tree'. Its unit of enforcement is the individual write/command, not a Stop-boundary claim measured against accumulated state. It also cannot replace pre_push_gate.py:78-107, the push-shape proof that refuses to auto-approve anything that is not provably a single current-branch push (it cross-checks push.default, @{upstream} vs @{push}, per-remote push refspecs, remote.mirror and push.followTags before trusting a bare `git push`).
alternatives.cost: Node.js + npm devDependency and a TypeScript probity.config.ts, in a repo whose hooks are deliberately stdlib Python with no install step; AI-validated rules spend agent tokens on every intercepted action
alternatives.maturity: the strongest-maintained alternative here. Verified from the repo page: MIT, 531 commits on main, active CI and security workflows, and it explicitly supersedes tdd-guard ('New projects should start there'). I did NOT verify the last commit date, the release cadence, the download count, or whether it runs on Windows.

alternatives.name: Claude Code native permissions.deny rules in settings.json (Anthropic, first-party)
alternatives.covers: the crude half of safety_gate.py with zero code: deny entries like Bash(rm:*) are checked before ask and before allow, first match wins, and --dangerously-skip-permissions does not bypass them. This is the officially documented mechanism for exactly this intent and needs no process spawn.
alternatives.gap: patterns match the literal command string, not parsed semantics -- so a prefix mismatch (/usr/bin/git vs git) or a command built from a variable slips through, the same class of failure my probe demonstrated against safety_gate.py's own regexes, with less room to fix it. It has no notion of a reason string beyond the rule, no credential-file heuristics, and cannot express any of pre_push_gate.py's or ship_gate_stop.py's stateful logic. A search result also surfaced anthropics/claude-code issue #18846, titled '[BUG] Bash permissions in settings.json not enforced - requires custom hook workaround' -- I did not open that issue and cannot say whether it is current, reproduced, or fixed; treat it as a lead, not a finding.
alternatives.cost: free, first-party, no runtime added, no dependency -- by far the cheapest option on this list
alternatives.maturity: first-party and documented at code.claude.com/docs; I did not verify the enforcement bug report's status, which is exactly the thing that would decide this.

alternatives.name: cchooks (GowayLee/cchooks, Python SDK) and cchook (syou6162/cchook, YAML-configured CLI)
alternatives.covers: the boilerplate half of all four files: stdin JSON parse, hook-type detection, typed contexts (PreToolUseContext etc.), and structured exit-code-or-JSON output. Every one of these hooks hand-rolls that: safety_gate.py:156-162, completion_gate.py:44-53, pre_push_gate.py:226-234 and ship_gate_stop.py:189-199 each re-implement 'read stdin, json.loads, fall open on garbage', and safety_gate.py:142-153 / pre_push_gate.py:212-223 each re-implement the hookSpecificOutput envelope.
alternatives.gap: it is a plumbing SDK -- it supplies no policy whatsoever. Every regex, the tree fingerprint, the ledger read, the proof validation and the push-shape checks stay exactly as much code as today. It would also convert a stdlib-only hook into one with a pip dependency that must import inside a 5-second PreToolUse timeout, and cchook's YAML/template model cannot express ship_gate_stop.py:65-91 (dynamically importing gate.py from three candidate deploy paths) or pre_push_gate.py:135-164 (shelling out to the prove-implementation validator and parsing its state JSON).
alternatives.cost: pip or Go binary install; replaces roughly 60 of 791 lines of envelope handling while adding an install step and an import cost per hook invocation
alternatives.maturity: not verified. Both appeared in search results with descriptions; I did not fetch either repo, so stars, licence, last release and Windows support are all unknown to me.

alternatives.name: Git-native pre-push hook via husky / lefthook / pre-commit (the standard practice this bypasses)
alternatives.covers: the intent of pre_push_gate.py at a lower and more reliable layer: git itself runs .git/hooks/pre-push for ANY push from any client, agent or human, whereas pre_push_gate.py only fires when the push arrives as a Claude Code Bash tool call. Running the test suite there is the documented, decades-old practice.
alternatives.gap: a git hook can only exit 0 or non-zero -- it cannot return Claude Code's permissionDecision 'ask', which is the entire output vocabulary of pre_push_gate.py (every one of its eight branches at :239-292 asks a human rather than deciding). It runs after the agent has already decided to push, sees no agent context, cannot explain a reason back into the model's turn, and is bypassed by --no-verify, which an agent can append. It also does not validate a stored proof artefact against the current commit+diff; it just re-runs commands, which is a different and more expensive contract.
alternatives.cost: husky = npm devDependency; lefthook = Go binary or npm; pre-commit = pip. All free. All add an install step to a repo whose hooks currently need nothing but the system Python.
alternatives.maturity: all three long-established and actively maintained per 2026 comparison articles found in search; I did not verify release dates or check any of their changelogs this session.

alternatives.name: Invariant Guardrails / NeMo Guardrails / AgentSpec (academic + commercial runtime enforcement for agent tool calls)
alternatives.covers: the general problem safety_gate.py is a hand-rolled instance of: intercepting a proposed agent action and applying a declarative policy before it executes. AgentSpec (ICSE 2026 paper found via search) formalises exactly this as customisable runtime enforcement; Invariant Guardrails ships it as a gateway/proxy between the agent and its LLM or MCP servers; NeMo Guardrails offers input/output/tool-call rails in Colang.
alternatives.gap: all three sit at the LLM/MCP network hop, not at the local Bash tool boundary -- Invariant's gateway is a proxy service between the app and the provider, which for first-party Claude Code OAuth would mean inserting a gateway the repo's own model-selection rule forbids. One of the surveyed sources states plainly that NeMo rails 'do not reason about multi-step sequences or shell-level obfuscation', which is precisely the failure my probe found. None of them has any concept of a git working tree, a commit hash, or an evidence ledger, so none can touch ship_gate_stop.py or pre_push_gate.py.
alternatives.cost: a running gateway service or a Colang policy layer plus its runtime, for a single-maintainer local CLI -- disproportionate, and for Invariant it means routing agent traffic through a third party
alternatives.maturity: Invariant Labs was acquired by/partnered with Snyk per a Snyk Labs page in results; NeMo Guardrails is NVIDIA-maintained; AgentSpec is a 2026 research artefact. I read only search summaries and did not fetch, install or evaluate any of the three.

evidence: Read in full: dot-claude/hooks/safety_gate.py:1-175, dot-claude/hooks/pre_push_gate.py:1-300, dot-claude/hooks/ship_gate_stop.py:1-245, dot-claude/hooks/completion_gate.py:1-75 (791 Python lines total, matching wc -l). Read dot-claude/settings.json hooks block to confirm actual wiring and timeouts (PreToolUse Bash -> safety_gate 5s then pre_push_gate 90s; Stop -> completion_gate 8s then ship_gate_stop 20s). Read docs/prior-art/tools-gate.json in full as the depth reference. Confirmed by cat that protect-infra.sh, session-context.sh, watchdog-verify.sh and coverage-enforcer.sh are each a single line containing /home/shovalbe/.codex/hooks/<name>.sh, a path that does not exist on this Windows machine -- the silent-fail-open precedent ship_gate_stop.py:28-31 was written against. RAN AN EXECUTABLE PROBE (scratchpad/probe_safety.py, six commands piped as hook JSON into safety_gate.py): 'rm -rf /', 'xargs -I{} rm -rf /', 'git    push   --force origin main' and 'Remove-Item -Recurse -Force C:\Users\shova' were all DENIED; 'T=/ ; rm -rf $T' and 'eval $(echo payload | base64 -d)' were ALLOWED. Six WebSearches across three vocabularies: practitioner (Claude Code PreToolUse deny guards; Stop hook completion-evidence blocking; native permissions.deny vs hooks), product (tdd-guard/probity; cchooks/cchook SDKs; husky/lefthook/pre-commit pre-push), academic (runtime enforcement / policy enforcement point for LLM agent tool calls, which surfaced AgentSpec ICSE26 and several 2026 arXiv surveys). Three WebFetches: the 04-stop-hook pattern README, claude-code-bash-guardian, and nizos/probity. NOT VERIFIED: I installed and ran nothing third-party. I did not read the source of any alternative, only READMEs and search summaries. Star counts, licences, last-commit dates and Windows support are unknown for cchooks, cchook, the 04-stop-hook pattern, and all three guardrail platforms. I did not open anthropics/claude-code issue #18846 and cannot say whether the permissions-enforcement bug it names is current. I did not measure how often, if ever, any of these four hooks has actually fired in a real session -- state/ has a ledger but I did not query it for hook-block events, so the operational value of each file is asserted from its code, not from usage data.
recheck: Run this to re-open the verdict, in this order. (1) The split's adopt half: `gh repo view RoaringFerrum/claude-code-bash-guardian --json stargazerCount,pushedAt,licenseInfo` and `gh repo view nizos/probity --json stargazerCount,pushedAt,licenseInfo` -- if bash-guardian is still ~7 stars / 3 commits, do not adopt it; instead lift only the technique with `python -c "import bashlex"` after `uv pip install bashlex` and back safety_gate.py's POSIX branch with an AST walk. (2) The keep half: `gh search code "tree_fingerprint" --language python` and `gh search code "diff_sha256" filename:*.py` plus WebSearch "claude code stop hook evidence git commit hash working tree fingerprint stale proof" -- if any maintained project binds agent evidence to a working-tree content hash rather than a time window, the keep half collapses and this becomes adopt. (3) The measured gap, rerun any time: `python C:/Users/shova/claude-setup/tools/gate/enforce_selftest.py` for the Stop-hook property, and re-run the six-case probe (variable-indirected and base64/eval deletion still returning allow means the AST work is still outstanding). (4) `gh issue view 18846 --repo anthropics/claude-code --json state,title` -- if native Bash permission enforcement is confirmed fixed, a chunk of safety_gate.py's git-destruction rules can move into settings.json deny entries and delete code.
what_ours_does: Four Python hooks wired in dot-claude/settings.json, plus twelve one-line shell files that are dead WSL paths and are not counted here. safety_gate.py (174) is a PreToolUse Bash deny-list of seventeen compiled regexes (safety_gate.py:18-139): three cover recursive deletion of broad/home/root/.git targets across POSIX rm, PowerShell Remove-Item -Recurse and cmd rd /s (:19-47); ten cover git history and worktree destruction -- reset --hard, clean -f, forced branch delete, force-push, refspec/mirror/prune push, checkout --, forced checkout, switch --discard-changes, restore without --staged (:48-100); one blocks piping a network response into a shell (:101-104); three block credential exfiltration into model-visible output via pagers, grep-family tools, or an interpreter one-liner reading .env/.ssh/*.pem/service-account JSON (:105-138). It is deliberately fail-open on malformed stdin (:156-162) so a broken guard cannot brick the CLI, and its own docstring (:6-8) states it is a guardrail, not an OS boundary. pre_push_gate.py (299) fires PreToolUse on Bash and ignores everything that is not a push (:236-238); anything other than a bare `git push` is escalated to a human 'ask' rather than reasoned about (:239-244). For a bare push it proves the push shape before trusting it -- staged files plus @{push}..HEAD, and it bails to __AMBIGUOUS_PUSH__ if push.default is not simple, if @{upstream} and @{push} disagree, if the remote has configured push refspecs, or if remote.mirror or push.followTags is set (:78-107). It classifies the resulting file list as source vs test through an explicit suffix/filename/prefix taxonomy that also treats CI workflows, migrations and .claude/hooks/ as behaviour-affecting (:17-42, :110-132). If source changed, it shells out to ~/.claude/skills/prove-implementation/scripts/implementation_proof.py to get the current {git_commit, diff_sha256} (:135-164) and then accepts .claude/proofs/current.json only if the schema matches AND at least one check passed with exit_code 0, a non-empty command and an output_sha256, AND every passing check's recorded repo_state equals the CURRENT commit and diff hash (:167-209). The three failure modes are distinct messages, and one of them says the load-bearing sentence out loud: 'Test-file presence alone is not execution evidence' (:286-292). ship_gate_stop.py (244) is the Stop-boundary counterpart: it walks up at most six levels for a quality-contract.json, stopping at the git root (:50-62), dynamically imports tools/gate/gate.py from CLAUDE_SETUP_ROOT or two known deploy layouts (:65-91), then asks whether state/gate-runs.jsonl holds a non-partial PASS row whose fingerprint equals gate.tree_fingerprint(project) right now (:154-186). It distinguishes four negative answers in its message -- never gated, gated-and-failed with the blocking domains named, only single domains run (partial), or gated against other trees only. It recovers the assistant's last message from the transcript file when the payload does not carry it inline (:94-136, and its docstring notes completion_gate.py reads only the inline keys), reuses completion_gate.COMPLETION by importing it so the two definitions cannot drift (:139-151), blocks with a runnable remediation command when a completion claim is present and merely emits a systemMessage otherwise (:230-240), and -- the design point -- emits a loud 'Ship gate is OFF' systemMessage rather than a silent pass whenever gate.py is unreachable or the ledger cannot be read (:210-221). completion_gate.py (74) is the cheap one: a Stop hook that blocks exactly once when a bilingual COMPLETION regex matches and a bilingual EVIDENCE regex does not (:12-28, :55-67), notable mainly for Hebrew claim/evidence terms guarded with Hebrew-codepoint lookarounds so they do not match inside longer words.
strongest_counterargument: The split is half cowardice and half overreach, and both halves deserve naming. Overreach: I am recommending an AST rewrite of safety_gate.py on the strength of a two-case probe against a 7-star, 3-commit repository I never installed. Regex incompleteness is real but it is also DOCUMENTED at safety_gate.py:6-8 and accepted by design -- the file explicitly says it is a guardrail behind native permissions, not an OS boundary, and the actual threat model is a cooperative agent making a careless call, not an adversary crafting `eval $(base64 -d)` to defeat its own operator's hook. Under that threat model my two allowed cases are curiosities, not defects, and swapping seventeen greppable regexes for a bashlex dependency inside a 5-second PreToolUse timeout on every Bash call trades a known small gap for an unknown import-cost and parse-failure surface, on a machine where the default shell is PowerShell and bashlex cannot parse the commands that actually run. Cowardice: I kept 543 lines by pointing at one property, working-tree binding, that only about forty of those lines implement. pre_push_gate.py is the weakest file in the directory by its own logic -- it fires only when a push arrives as a Claude Code Bash tool call, so an agent that runs `git push --no-verify`, a wrapper, a different repo, or any push at all from outside Claude Code simply escapes it, and its own answer to that is to punt to 'ask' in eight of eight non-trivial branches. A hook whose dominant output is 'ask a human' is a permission prompt with 299 lines of preamble, and a git-native pre-push hook would cover the push path more completely for a fraction of the code. The genuinely irreplaceable core of this directory is ship_gate_stop.py's ledger check plus the fail-loud branch: call it 90 lines. A harsher and defensible verdict is that 700 of the 791 lines are replaceable or deletable, and that this record chose the comfortable split because deleting completion_gate.py outright -- which ship_gate_stop.py's own docstring argues for in four sentences -- would have required admitting a wired, running Stop hook is theatre.
